title: Phylogenetic Species Atlas: species-level phylogenies of eukaryotes and the coverage of described species
description:
A catalogue of 263 published species-level phylogenies: the largest species-level tree found for each of 24 groups of described eukaryotes and for Bacteria and Archaea (26 reference trees), and 237 other trees, among them 218 family-level trees of tetrapods. 255 of them are redistributed as Newick files with numeric tip ids, each under the licence of its source (LICENSE-trees.md, generated from registers/tree_licences.csv); the other 8, whose sources state no licence (cephalopods, frogs, gastropods, insects, primates, seed plants, sharks and sponges), are listed in registers/withheld_trees.csv with the source to download each from, the sha256 and tip count of the file the paper used and how it was derived, and their tip lists are in registers/withheld_tips/. A name layer resolves every tip id to a standardized name and every reference-tree tip to a Catalogue of Life accepted name (COL26.9 base release, ChecklistBank 316321).

Registers record, for each reference tree, the tips removed as outside its group, the tips in the molecular analysis behind it (with the alignment taxa lists and source-tree tip lists they are derived from), whether it is a chronogram in absolute time, the divergence-time interval its source archive carries for the focal crown, and the calibration on that node. From them the 2,085,607 described eukaryotic species, divided into 60 groups, are counted at four nested levels: named in a reference tree, placed with molecular data, in a chronogram in absolute time, and in a chronogram whose archive carries date uncertainty a user can propagate (a tree set or node intervals).

scripts/reproduce_paper.py (Python standard library) recomputes every number, table and figure datum of the accompanying paper from these files and compares it with the paper's generated inputs (paper/); code/rebuild holds the pipeline that wrote them. Companion to: Richter F., Described eukaryotic species in published species-level phylogenies: placement by molecular data, dates and date uncertainty, bioRxiv doi:10.64898/2026.05.31.729127.

Licences: the catalogue's own work (registers, name layer, code, generated files, site) is CC BY 4.0; each tree file keeps the licence of its source: CC0 1.0, CC BY 4.0 or CC BY 2.0, the GTDB trees bacteria.nwk and archaea.nwk CC BY-SA 4.0, salamanders.nwk GPL-3.0 (LICENSES/GPL-3.0.txt). The source trees and alignments remain in their original archives (Dryad, Zenodo, Figshare, GitHub, VertLife, FishTreeOfLife, insectphylo, GTDB), cited in registers/tree_provenance.csv and in the headers of the derived files. The TimeTree of Life (Hedges et al. 2015) is cited and not redistributed, at the TimeTree project's request. Branch lengths in releases v1.0.3 to v1.0.8 are corrupted (ERRATUM.md); this release carries the corrected files.

Cite the version DOI of the release you used; the concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20127157 refers to all versions.
